name: smart_1_raw
variation: Often stable; may increase slowly with age. Sudden jumps are concerning.
notes: Raw value often includes both errors and total reads—encoding varies by vendor. Not always predictive.

name: smart_2_raw
variation: Typically stable; obsolete on modern drives.
notes: Rarely used today; mostly historical. Ignore on modern drives.

name: smart_3_raw
variation: Stable over life; increases if motor weakens.
notes: Measured in milliseconds; rising values suggest aging motor or power issues.

name: smart_4_raw
variation: Increases only when powered on/off; should be much less than power cycle count.
notes: High counts normal in laptops or frequently cycled systems—but excessive cycling adds wear.

name: smart_5_raw
variation: Should be 0; any increase indicates media degradation.
notes: Critical attribute. Non-zero means sectors have failed and been remapped.

name: smart_7_raw
variation: May be high but stable; sharp rise suggests mechanical issues.
notes: Often a ratio (errors/total seeks). High raw doesn’t always mean failure—check trend.

name: smart_8_raw
variation: Obsolete; usually constant.
notes: Not used in modern drives. Ignore unless on legacy hardware.

name: smart_9_raw
variation: Steadily increases (~8760 hrs/year at 24/7). Not a failure predictor by itself.
notes: Useful for estimating drive age and usage intensity.

name: smart_10_raw
variation: Should be 0; any value indicates motor or power issues.
notes: Retries occur when drive fails to spin up normally—sign of impending failure.

name: smart_11_raw
variation: Should be 0; non-zero suggests servo or mechanical problems.
notes: Indicates drive had trouble calibrating head position—rare but serious.

name: smart_12_raw
variation: Increases with each power cycle; high counts normal in servers.
notes: Compare with POH: frequent cycling in short time may stress components.

name: smart_13_raw
variation: Corrected errors; moderate values OK if stable.
notes: Errors corrected via ECC—concerning only if rising rapidly.

name: smart_22_raw
variation: Should be stable; drop indicates seal leak (enterprise helium-filled drives).
notes: Only on enterprise helium-sealed drives (e.g., WD Ultrastar, Seagate Exos). A drop = potential failure.

name: smart_170_raw
description: Reserved Block Count / Program Fail Count
variation: Varies by vendor: may show used or remaining blocks.
notes: Samsung: shows used spares → lower = better. Others may show remaining → higher = better.

name: smart_171_raw
variation: Should be 0; any increase is serious.
notes: Failed NAND program (write) operations—indicates wear or defect.

name: smart_172_raw
variation: Should be 0; indicates NAND wear or defect.
notes: Failed block erasures—bad sign for SSD health.

name: smart_173_raw
variation: May show max-min erase cycles (lower = better) or % life remaining (higher = better).
notes: Samsung: lower = more even wear. Intel/Micron: may show % life left. Vendor-specific!

name: smart_174_raw
variation: Increases only on unsafe shutdowns; should be rare.
notes: Sudden power loss can corrupt data or FTL metadata—use UPS if frequent.

name: smart_175_raw
variation: Cumulative; should be 0 or very low.
notes: Total write failures over lifetime—any value warrants monitoring.

name: smart_176_raw
variation: Cumulative; should be 0.
notes: Same as above for erase operations.

name: smart_177_raw
variation: Lower = more even wear; increases slowly over time.
notes: Difference between most/least worn blocks—high delta = poor wear leveling.

name: smart_178_raw
variation: Increases as spare blocks are consumed; sudden rise = bad.
notes: Spare blocks being used—non-zero is normal late in life, but rapid increase = concern.

name: smart_179_raw
variation: Decreases over time; should not reach 0.
notes: Remaining spares—critical buffer before drive goes read-only.

name: smart_180_raw
variation: Total spare blocks remaining; higher is better.
notes: Similar to 179; total pool of spares.

name: smart_181_raw
description: Program Fail Count / Non-4K Aligned Access
variation: Should be low; depends on workload alignment.
notes: On some drives, reflects misaligned I/O—which increases write amplification.

name: smart_182_raw
description: Erase Fail Count / Initial Bad Block
variation: Initial bad blocks are normal; new failures are not.
notes: All NAND has factory bad blocks—only new failures matter.

name: smart_183_raw
variation: Should be 0; occasional downshifts may be harmless (cable issue).
notes: Drive fell back to SATA I/II due to signal integrity—check cables/power.

name: smart_184_raw
variation: Should be 0; any value indicates cache-to-disk mismatch.
notes: IBM/Hitachi attribute—data corruption between cache and platter.

name: smart_187_raw
variation: Critical: Should be 0; any value means data loss occurred.
notes: High-priority warning. Data could not be recovered—backup and replace drive.

name: smart_188_raw
variation: Should be 0; may indicate cable, power, or controller issues.
notes: Commands took too long—often due to loose SATA cable or insufficient power.

name: smart_189_raw
variation: Should be 0; indicates head flying too high during writes.
notes: Head wasn’t close enough to disk—writes may be unreliable.

name: smart_190_raw
variation: Varies with environment; sustained >50°C is risky.
notes: Some vendors use this for temp; others use 194. Avoid prolonged high temps.

name: smart_191_raw
variation: Increases with physical shocks; should be 0 in stable environments.
notes: Logs events where accelerometer detected shock (common in laptops).

name: smart_192_raw
variation: Increases on unsafe shutdowns; normal if occasional.
notes: Number of times heads were emergency-parked due to power loss.

name: smart_193_raw
variation: Increases with head parking; high counts normal in laptops.
notes: Heads unload to save power—rated for 300k–600k cycles. Excessive = wear.

name: smart_194_raw
variation: Typical range: 20–45°C; spikes under load are normal.
notes: Most common temp attribute. Sustained >60°C reduces lifespan.

name: smart_195_raw
variation: Moderate values OK; rising trend indicates marginal sectors.
notes: Corrected sector errors—OK if stable, bad if climbing.

name: smart_196_raw
variation: Should be 0; tracks reallocation attempts.
notes: Counts attempts to remap sectors—even if successful, it’s a red flag.

name: smart_197_raw
variation: Critical: Should be 0; sectors awaiting remap—urgent if >0.
notes: Imminent failure risk. These sectors failed read but haven’t been remapped yet.

name: smart_198_raw
variation: Critical: Should be 0; uncorrectable errors found offline.
notes: Found during self-test—means permanent data loss on those sectors.

name: smart_199_raw
variation: Should be 0; indicates cable or interface issues.
notes: Almost always due to faulty SATA cable or port—try replacing cable first.

name: smart_200_raw
variation: On SSDs: may reflect wear—increases with use.
notes: On HDDs: write errors. On SSDs: may show total program/erase cycles.

name: smart_201_raw
variation: Should be 0; indicates read instability.
notes: Errors that couldn’t be fixed by ECC—sector likely failing.

name: smart_202_raw
variation: Should be 0; media or timing issue.
notes: Rare; suggests timing or media flaw.

name: smart_203_raw
variation: Should be 0; servo problem.
notes: Servo couldn’t complete operation—mechanical issue.

name: smart_204_raw
variation: Low/moderate is normal; rising trend is bad.
notes: Similar to 195—corrected errors. Monitor trend.

name: smart_205_raw
variation: Should be 0; head-disk contact due to heat.
notes: Caused by thermal protrusion—can damage media.

name: smart_206_raw
variation: Stable value expected; deviations indicate problems.
notes: Measures head-to-disk distance—instability = risk of crash.

name: smart_207_raw
variation: Should be low; increases if motor degrades.
notes: High current draw during spin-up = motor strain.

name: smart_208_raw
variation: Should be 0; failed spin attempts.
notes: Drive tried and failed to spin—serious mechanical issue.

name: smart_209_raw
variation: Obsolete; usually constant.
notes: Legacy attribute—ignore on modern drives.

name: smart_210_raw
variation: Should be 0; indicates external vibration.
notes: Logged if vibration sensor triggered during write.

name: smart_211_raw
variation: Should be 0.
notes: Same as above for read operations.

name: smart_212_raw
variation: Should be 0; physical shock events.
notes: Sudden movement during write—risk of head crash.

name: smart_220_raw
variation: Should be 0; mechanical misalignment.
notes: Physical shift of platters—usually after impact.

name: smart_221_raw
variation: Same as smart_191_raw.
notes: Alternate ID for shock events.

name: smart_222_raw
variation: Increases with head loaded time; normal in always-on drives.
notes: Time heads were in contact with disk—complements load/unload count.

name: smart_223_raw
variation: Should be 0; retries indicate actuator issues.
notes: Failed to park/unpark head—mechanical wear.

name: smart_224_raw
variation: Should be low; increases with wear.
notes: Measures resistance during loading—rising = aging.

name: smart_225_raw
variation: Same as smart_193_raw.
notes: Alternate counter for head cycles.

name: smart_226_raw
variation: Cumulative; increases with usage.
notes: Total time heads were loaded—usage metric.

name: smart_227_raw
variation: Should be 0; motor stress events.
notes: Excessive torque needed—motor or bearing issue.

name: smart_228_raw
variation: Same as smart_192_raw.
notes: Alternate power-off retract counter.

name: smart_230_raw
variation: On SSDs: may show % life used—increases with wear.
notes: On HDDs: head signal strength. On SSDs (e.g., Samsung): life used %.

name: smart_231_raw
variation: Often 100→0 scale; decreases with use. Some vendors show temperature.
notes: Samsung: shows % life left → higher = better. Others may show temp. Always check vendor!

name: smart_232_raw
variation: Decreases over time; critical when near 0.
notes: Spare block pool—when exhausted, drive may go read-only.

name: smart_233_raw
variation: Intel: 100 = new, 1 = worn out; decreases with use.
notes: Intel/Micron standard: higher = healthier. Critical for endurance tracking.

name: smart_234_raw
variation: Spare blocks remaining; higher is better.
notes: Similar to 179/180—remaining spares.

name: smart_235_raw
variation: If writes: increases; if failures: should be 0.
notes: May represent total NAND writes (info) or failure count (bad)—vendor dependent.

name: smart_240_raw
variation: If hours: increases; if errors: should be 0.
notes: On HDDs: flying time. On some SSDs: transfer errors—interpret accordingly.

name: smart_241_raw
variation: Steadily increases with write activity.
notes: Useful for calculating drive wear (especially SSDs).

name: smart_242_raw
variation: Steadily increases with read activity.
notes: No direct health impact, but useful for workload analysis.

name: smart_243_raw
variation: Same as smart_241_raw.
notes: Redundant or extended counter on some drives.

name: smart_244_raw
variation: Increases with P/E cycles; rate indicates write intensity.
notes: Average number of erase cycles per block—key for wear estimation.

name: smart_245_raw
variation: Delta shows wear leveling effectiveness.
notes: Large difference = uneven wear = shorter lifespan.

name: smart_246_raw
variation: Increases with host writes.
notes: Same as 241 but in GB or sectors—varies by vendor.

name: smart_247_raw
variation: Increases with host reads.

name: smart_248_raw
variation: Higher than host writes due to write amplification.
notes: Internal writes = host writes × (1 + WA). High WA = inefficient controller.

name: smart_249_raw
variation: Cumulative writes; used for endurance estimation.
notes: Intel-specific—helps estimate remaining life based on TBW rating.

name: smart_250_raw
variation: Should be low; increasing trend = media degradation.
notes: Retries before giving up—rising count = failing media.

name: smart_251_raw
variation: Same as smart_241_raw.
notes: Alternate counter.

name: smart_252_raw
variation: Should be 0; indicates permanent data loss.
notes: Similar to 187—critical error.

name: smart_254_raw
variation: Increases with drop events; should be 0 in desktops.
notes: Found in laptop/mobile drives—counts free-fall protection triggers.
